chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Abū al-Ḥakam, who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ibrāhīm al-Jaʿfarī and ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmārah narrated to me from Yazīd ibn Salīṭ, who said:

When Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام made his bequest, he had as witnesses Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Jaʿfarī, Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Jaʿfarī, Isḥāq ibn Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, Jaʿfar ibn Ṣāliḥ, Muʿāwiyah al-Jaʿfarī, Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Saʿd ibn ʿImrān al-Anṣārī, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith al-Anṣārī, Yazīd ibn Salīṭ al-Anṣārī, and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Saʿd al-Aslamī, and he was the scribe of the bequest.

First, he made them witnesses that he testified that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner for Him; that Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله is His servant and His Messenger; that the Hour is coming, in which there is no doubt; that Allah will raise those in the graves; that resurrection after death is true; that the promise is true; that the reckoning is true; that the decree is true; that standing before Allah is true; that what Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله brought is true; and that what the Trustworthy Spirit brought down is true. Upon that I live, upon it I die, and upon it I shall be raised, if Allah wills.

And he made them witnesses that this is my bequest in my own handwriting. I have copied the bequest of my grandfather Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, and the bequest of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī; before that I copied it letter for letter; and the bequest of Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad was likewise. I have bequeathed to ʿAlī, and then my sons are with him: if he wills, and perceives right guidance in them, and wishes to confirm them, then that belongs to him; and if he dislikes them and wishes to remove them, then that belongs to him, and they have no authority alongside him.

And I have bequeathed to him my charities, my wealth, my mawālī, my young children whom I leave behind, and my children—Ibrāhīm, al-ʿAbbās, Qāsim, Ismāʿīl, Aḥmad, and Umm Aḥmad. The matter of my women, apart from them, belongs to ʿAlī. Also, a third of my father’s charity and my own third: he may place it wherever he sees fit and dispose within it as an owner disposes in his property. If he wishes to sell, gift, grant, or give it in charity to those whom I have named for him or to others besides those whom I named, that belongs to him. He is as myself in my bequest regarding my property, my family, and my children.

And if he sees fit to retain his brothers whom I have named in this document, he may retain them; and if he dislikes that, then he may remove them, without blame upon him and without his decision being reversed. If he perceives in them something different from what I left them upon, and wishes to return them into authority, that belongs to him. If one of them wishes to marry off his sister, he may not marry her off except with his permission and his command, for he is more knowledgeable of the marriages of his people.

And whichever ruler or any person among the people prevents him from anything, or stands between him and anything of what I have mentioned in this document or anyone whom I mentioned, then he is free of Allah and of His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger are free of him. Upon him is the curse of Allah, His wrath, the curse of those who curse, of the angels brought near, of the Prophets, of the Messengers, and of the body of the believers.

No ruler has the right to prevent him from anything. I have no claim against him, nor any liability, nor does any of my children have any property claim upon him before me. He is to be believed in what he states: if he gives less, he knows best, and if he gives more, then he is truthful in that as well. I only intended, by including those of my children whom I included with him, to mention their names publicly and to honor them.

As for the mothers of my children, whichever of them remains in her residence and in her seclusion, she shall have what used to be provided to her during my lifetime, if he sees fit. Whichever of them goes out to a husband may not return to my dwelling unless ʿAlī sees otherwise. My daughters are likewise. None of my daughters may be married off by any of their brothers through their mothers, nor by any ruler, nor by any paternal uncle, except by his judgment and consultation.

If they do otherwise than that, then they have opposed Allah and His Messenger and contended against Him in His dominion. He is more knowledgeable of the marriages of his people. If he wishes to marry them off, he does so; and if he wishes to leave it, he leaves it. I have instructed them with what I mentioned in this document, and I have made Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a witness over them; and He and Umm Aḥmad are two witnesses. No one has the right to uncover my bequest or spread it, acting regarding it other than what I have mentioned and specified.
So whoever does evil, it is against himself, and whoever does good, it is for himself, and your Lord is not unjust to the servants.

And may Allah send blessings upon Muḥammad and upon his family. No ruler or anyone else has the right to open this document of mine, upon which I have placed the lower seal. Whoever does that, upon him is the curse of Allah, His wrath, the curse of those who curse, of the angels brought near, of the company of the Messengers, and of the believers from among the Muslims, and upon whoever opens this document of mine. Abū Ibrāhīm wrote and sealed it, and the witnesses as well. And may Allah send blessings upon Muḥammad and upon his family.
Abū al-Ḥakam said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ādam al-Jaʿfarī narrated to me from Yazīd ibn Salīṭ, who said:

Abū ʿImrān al-Ṭalḥī was the judge of al-Madīnah. When Mūsā passed away, his brothers brought the matter before al-Ṭalḥī the judge. Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mūsā said: 'May Allah set you right and benefit through you. At the bottom of this document there is a treasure and jewels, and he wants to conceal it and take it for himself apart from us. Our father, may Allah have mercy on him, left nothing but that he consigned it to him, and left us burdened. Had I not restrained myself, I would have informed you of something before the heads of the assembly.'

Then Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad sprang toward him and said: 'Then, by Allah, you would be speaking of something we neither accept from you nor believe you in; then you would be among us blameworthy and cast off. We have known you for lying in youth and old age, and your father knew you better—had there been any good in you. Your father knew you outwardly and inwardly, and he would not have trusted you even with two dates.'

Then Isḥāq ibn Jaʿfar, his paternal uncle, leapt toward him and seized him by his collar and said to him: 'You are foolish, weak, and stupid. Add this to what came from you yesterday.' All the people supported him. Then Abū ʿImrān the judge said to ʿAlī: 'Stand, O Abū al-Ḥasan. Enough for me is what your father cursed me with today. Your father gave broad authority to you, and by Allah, no one knows a child better than his father. By Allah, your father was not considered by us light in intellect nor weak in judgment.'

Al-ʿAbbās said to the judge: 'May Allah set you right, break the seal and read what is beneath it.' Abū ʿImrān said: 'I will not break it; enough for me is what your father cursed me with today.' Al-ʿAbbās said: 'Then I will open it myself.' He said: 'That is up to you.' So al-ʿAbbās broke the seal, and there it contained their removal, and the confirmation of it for ʿAlī alone, and their being placed under the authority of ʿAlī whether they liked or disliked it, and their exclusion from the bounds of the charity and other matters. Its opening became for them an affliction, disgrace, and humiliation, while for ʿAlī عليه السلام it was a matter of choice and distinction.

And in the bequest that al-ʿAbbās opened beneath the seal were these witnesses: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad, Isḥāq ibn Jaʿfar, Jaʿfar ibn Ṣāliḥ, and Saʿīd ibn ʿImrān. They exposed the face of Umm Aḥmad in the judge’s gathering and claimed that she was not the one in question until they uncovered her and recognized her. At that point she said: 'By Allah, my master had indeed said this: you will be taken by force and brought out to the assemblies.' Then Isḥāq ibn Jaʿfar rebuked her and said: 'Be silent, for women are prone to weakness; I do not think he said anything of this.'

Then ʿAlī عليه السلام turned to al-ʿAbbās and said: 'My brother, I know that what has driven you to this is the liabilities and debts upon you. Go, O Saʿīd, and ascertain for me what is upon them, then pay it off on their behalf. No, by Allah, I will not cease to support you and deal kindly with you as long as I walk upon the earth. So say whatever you wish.'

Al-ʿAbbās said: 'You only give us from the excess of our own wealth, and what we have with you is more.' He said: 'Say whatever you wish; your honor is your own. If you do good, that is for you with Allah; and if you do evil, then Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. By Allah, you know that as of this day I have no child and no heir other than you. If I have withheld or stored up anything of what you suppose, it is only for you and will return to you. By Allah, since your father passed away—may Allah be pleased with him—I have possessed nothing except that I have released it where you saw.'

Then al-ʿAbbās sprang up and said: 'By Allah, it is not so. Allah has not given you any authority of judgment over us. Rather, it was our father’s envy toward us and his intention of what Allah has not allowed for him nor for you. And you know well that I know Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, the seller of sābirī cloth in Kūfah; if I remain safe, I will choke him with his own saliva, and you along with him.'

Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: 'There is no power and no strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. As for me, my brothers, I am eager for your happiness—Allah knows. O Allah, if You know that I love their well-being, that I am dutiful to them, maintaining ties with them, gentle toward them, and attentive to their affairs night and day, then recompense me for it with good. But if I am otherwise than that, then You are the Knower of the unseen, so recompense me according to what I deserve: if it be evil, then evil; and if it be good, then good.'

O Allah, rectify them and rectify matters for them, drive away Shayṭān from us and from them, help them to obey You, and grant them success toward Your right guidance. As for me, my brother, I am eager for your happiness and striving for your well-being, and Allah is Trustee over what we say.'
Al-ʿAbbās said: 'How well I know your tongue, but your shovel has no clay with me.'
Then the people parted upon this, and may Allah send blessings upon Muḥammad and his family.

key_terms.السَّاعَةَ: the Hour, meaning the coming Day of Resurrection
key_terms.الْحِسَابَ: the reckoning of deeds before Allah
key_terms.صَدَقَاتِي: my charitable endowments or properties set aside in charity
key_terms.لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ: the curse of Allah invoked upon violators of the bequest
key_terms.مَنَاكِحِ: marriage arrangements and suitable matrimonial matches
key_terms.وَلَايَةِ: authority or guardianship entrusted to ʿAlī عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What does the will of Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام say about the authority of ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام and the dispute after his father’s death?
ai.summary: This narration preserves the detailed text of the will of Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام and the events that followed its presentation before the judge of al-Madīnah. It combines creedal testimony, designation of authority to ʿAlī عليه السلام, directives on property and family matters, and a later dispute among the Imam’s sons that publicly confirmed the contents of the will.
